title: For a developer
reader: a senior engineer who builds with AI agents every day
judges: Is it accurate, can I reproduce it, and are the controls implementable as described?
why_you: You build with agents every day. If a control here hides work, or a number cannot be rerun from the record, you are the reader who will try it and find out.

chapters_note: A proposal by developer@, from the reviewers study's themes for this reader; which length every page aims at is the editor's question.

questions.q: Which control could you implement as described, and which hides work the page does not show?
What failure mode did the team miss: tool scope, shared state, memory, instructions in material?
Where does a check depend on the agent running it on itself? Does the chapter say so plainly?
Is any passage closer to a method than to a risk? Mark it.
Pick one number and rerun it. Did you get the same result?
Is each command clear enough to run without asking anyone?
Which number's definition would you argue with?
What is missing for you to trust the rest of the book's numbers?
